newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber thin, waits for Thai cabinet meet.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber thin, waits for Thai cabinet meet.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was thin by midday on Tuesday with the trade waiting for news on a Thai cabinet meeting to yield news on a rubber deal with China, dealers said.
"Some of us are waiting for the Thai cabinet meeting to see if something will come out that will affect the rubber trade," a dealer said.

"It's pretty much like the morning markets we've had lately where nothing happens and everybody waits for the afternoon session so they can take their lead from the performance of the Japanese rubber market," another trader said.
Higher prices in Tokyo, where the key October contract climbed 1.3 yen in the morning to 140.6 failed to lift local sentiment, dealers said.
There may have been some sporadic deals for RSS3 rubber, but action in all other rubber grades remained slim.
At 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 109.50 U.S. cents a kg from 109.00 cents.
June RSS1 was indicated at 156.75 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 157.50 cents. June TSR20 was indicated at 153.00-155.00 Singapore cents (US$1.06-$1.08) a kg from 151.75 cents.
